skill.name: listening-script
skill.description: Adapt articles, research reports, book notes, and AI drafts into narration that works without a screen. Preserve evidence, uncertainty, numbers, and separate source notes.
skill.summary: Turn source material into listening scripts while preserving attribution, numerical accuracy, and evidence limits.
skill.author: godgod126

security_audit.summary: Static analysis supplied no findings, so no finding verdicts are required. The two reviewed files describe text adaptation and explicitly prohibit credential requests and additional service uploads. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions.

content.user_title: Create Listening Scripts That Preserve Evidence
content.value_statement: Screen-oriented articles and reports can be difficult to follow aloud without losing important evidence. This skill adapts them into narration with clear comparisons, audible uncertainty, and separate source notes.
actual_capabilities: Adapt supplied text into a title, plain-text narration body, and separate source or editorial notes.
Convert tables and visual references into spoken comparisons that preserve units, baselines, dates, and exceptions.
Explain formulas through quantities and relationships, retaining exact formulas in notes when needed.
Keep attribution, uncertainty, negative results, sample sizes, and hypothetical examples explicit.
Preserve continuity and glossary consistency across long sections while identifying partial coverage.
Compare narration against the source for changed numbers, causality, qualifiers, attribution, and omissions.
limitations: Produces text only; it does not synthesize audio, publish recordings, install software, or access accounts.
Does not independently verify supplied AI drafts or fill missing evidence with invented details.
Estimates audio duration from word count and delivery rate rather than measuring a recording.
May adapt only part of a long source; covered sections and substantial omissions must be stated.

use_cases.title: Prepare article narration
use_cases.description: Adapt a source-backed article for listening while retaining spoken attribution and moving detailed references into separate notes.

use_cases.title: Explain research comparisons aloud
use_cases.description: Convert report tables into spoken comparisons without removing sample limits, negative results, or uncertainty.

use_cases.title: Create accessible study narration
use_cases.description: Turn book notes or technical reading into consistent narration with clarified acronyms and verbal explanations of formulas.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a short article
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the supplied article into an English listening script. Preserve its claims and detail. Return a title, narration, and separate source notes. Source: [article]
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a first narration draft.

prompt_templates.title: Narrate a comparison table
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this paragraph and table into spoken narration for [audience]. Preserve units, baselines, sample sizes, exceptions, and uncertainty. Record omissions separately. Source: [text and table]
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: explain visual data without overstating results.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt technical material
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt [technical source] into [language] narration for [audience]. Explain formulas verbally and retain exact forms in notes. Preserve attribution and qualifiers. Target length: [word count].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare technical narration with separate reference material.

prompt_templates.title: Maintain a long report across sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt [report] section by section using [glossary] and [voice]. Preserve detail and evidence limits. State coverage and omissions. Check numbers, causality, attribution, and qualifiers before delivery.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain continuity and source fidelity across a long document.

output_examples.input: Adapt this fictional test into narration: twelve devices tested once per version; median waits were ten seconds for A and eight for B. Three devices favored A; battery use and user preferences were not measured.
output: Title: A Preliminary Comparison of Waiting Times
Narration: In a preliminary test, twelve devices ran the same passage once with each version.
Version A had a median wait of ten seconds, compared with eight seconds for version B.
That is a two-second reduction, or twenty percent relative to A.
Three devices were faster with A, so B was not faster on every device.
Battery use and user preferences were not measured.
Source notes: This example is fictional. It does not establish battery savings or user preference.

output_examples.input: Adapt this supplied sentence for listening: The table above estimates an increase from 10 to 12 requests per minute in this sample.
output: Narration: In this sample, the estimated request rate increased from ten to twelve requests per minute.
That is an increase of two requests per minute, or twenty percent relative to the starting rate.
Source notes: The estimate applies only to the stated sample. The supplied text gives no sample size or measurement date.

best_practices: Supply source text and references, then specify audience, language, length, voice, and permitted editorial changes.
Keep narration separate from source notes, exact formulas, raw URLs, and unresolved editorial questions.
Review numbers, attribution, qualifiers, and omissions against the source before using the script.
anti_patterns: Requesting a listening adaptation while silently expecting major summarization or unsupported additions.
Turning a preliminary benchmark into a universal claim, product recommendation, or verified user outcome.
Treating a text script as synthesized audio or its estimated duration as a measured recording.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate audio?
faq.answer: No. It produces narration text that you can use separately with a text-to-speech tool or a human narrator.

faq.question: Does it summarize the source automatically?
faq.answer: No. Making text listenable does not authorize summarization. Specify your desired length and any permitted compression.

faq.question: How does it handle tables and formulas?
faq.answer: It converts tables into spoken relationships and explains formulas verbally. Exact formulas and omitted details can remain in separate notes.

faq.question: Does it independently fact-check AI drafts?
faq.answer: No. It preserves source boundaries and flags unresolved claims. New research uses only available, authorized tools and sources.

faq.question: How does it handle long documents?
faq.answer: It maintains continuity and glossary consistency across sections. If processing is partial, it states coverage rather than implying the entire document was adapted.
